task: CS2 human-like Deathmatch bot — math/algorithms for simultaneous movement + shooting

tech_stack.navigation_yaw_pitch_predictor: RepViT M1.5 (returns spatial coords + yaw/pitch on maps)

hypothesis_tree.claim: Human aiming is decomposable into a primary ballistic submovement + corrective submovements (Meyer/Crossman-Goodeve / WHo model).
supporting: Meyer 1988 'Optimality in human motor performance' iso-vu model
hypothesis_tree.consequences: We can synthesize aim curves as a sum of overlapping bell-shaped speed profiles (Sigma-Lognormal); produces both ballistic + corrective phases.

hypothesis_tree.claim: Mouse path geometry is well modelled by Bezier curves perturbed by Perlin/OU noise with constant-jerk timing.
supporting: Bezmouse / pyclick / GhostCursor / WindMouse algorithm by Benjamin J. Land (Aldaron) 2007
hypothesis_tree.consequences: Use 3rd-order Bezier between current and target with noise overlay; reparameterize time with min-jerk profile.

hypothesis_tree.claim: Counter-strafe accuracy mechanic in CS2 is the dominant constraint on simultaneous movement+shooting.
supporting: Valve developer wiki on weapon_accuracy_nospread / inaccuracy
CS2 movement inaccuracy decay constants from cs_weapon_data
hypothesis_tree.consequences: Bot must press opposite key for ~50–80 ms before shooting (A then D, etc.) to zero velocity, then re-press.

hypothesis_tree.claim: PID/Kalman fusion of RepViT yaw/pitch (low-frequency, prior) with YOLO target offsets (high-frequency, evidence) yields stable aim.
supporting: Standard sensor-fusion / Kalman Filter literature; complementary filter alternative
hypothesis_tree.consequences: Treat RepViT as process model, YOLO measurement; tune Q/R to taste.

hypothesis_tree.claim: Reaction-time noise (200–250 ms median) and overshoot ratio (~5–10 %) must be sampled to defeat anti-cheat heuristics and bot-detection by ML.
hypothesis_tree.consequences: Sample reaction delay from ex-Gaussian (mu, sigma, tau) before triggering aim+fire.
